cv-hermitian-norms: Combines HasGram/IsGram, slope_sq, slopeMax_sq, Formalism.HN.muDef, Formalism.HN.ht and Formalism.DivisionValues.lcv. A norm system in the Lean is a function on all embeddings K -> C, constrained only at the chosen embedding v.embedding of each infinite place; slope_sq is muDef for a chosen Gram basis and 0 if there is none. Formalism.F.covol is defined as 0 when the image is not discrete, and Real.log 0 = 0. The identity lcv = -rk(L) mu(L) is a computation from the definitions (r = [K:Q]/2), proved here; the Lean uses it inside GlobalTheory.CovolCore.lcv_div_le_neg_slope_sq. The slope mu is twice the normalized Arakelov slope. In the Lean a metric is a family of matrices indexed by the infinite places, such as (p.S false).XW j; Chapter 8 uses the same name for it.
cv-rescaling: Same statement as GlobalTheory.T.covolumePerRank_le_neg_slope_scaled (proved by GlobalTheory.CovolCore.lcv_div_le_neg_slope_sq). The proof follows the Lean: the metric sX differs from X by the constant s (MeasureLeaf.lcv_of_oneConstant), lcv = -rk mu for it (ExtensionFiltration.lcvMu), and beta carries the realized lattice isometrically onto L (rk_deg_transport), so the slopes agree.
cv-slope-base-change: Part (1) is GlobalTheory.SlopeExt.slope_sq_sub_le_slope_sq_span (with its statement GlobalTheory.T.slope_sq_sub_le_slope_sq_span), part (2) is GlobalTheory.T.maxSlope_sq_fieldExtension_le_comparable_norms, proved by GlobalTheory.SlopeMaxExt.slopeMax_sq_span_le. The Lean also assumes that N and N' have Gram bases (HasGram) and that L is finitely generated. The proof of (1) follows the Lean: rk_mul_mu_eq for both lattices is the slope formula at the start of the proof, relIndex_span with card_tensor gives the index [L:L_0]^[K':K], gram_le compares the Gram determinants, and sum_comap sums over the extensions of each embedding. The proof of (2) follows slopeMax_sq_span_le: it passes to the normal closure F with rescaled norms (exists_frame, coordExt), applies (1) to the maximal-slope sublattice, and uses GlobalTheory.T.maxSlope_extendedLattice_galois_le for the Galois extension F/K, proved by GlobalTheory.SlopeGal.slopeMax_sq_span_le, which the text follows: exists_top_step gives the sublattice M of largest rank among those of maximal slope, the Galois twists tw keep it (rk_deg_image with norm_realize_gal), so its span W is Galois stable and M = L' cap W is the extension of L cap iota^-1(W) (inf_eq_span), and slope_sq_span_le compares the two slopes. In the covolume bound, (1) gives Proposition cv-point-conditions(5) inside GlobalTheory.CoreSlope.coreAt_of and (2) gives the bound for mu_max(Lambda^all) inside GlobalTheory.CovTop.LamAll.slopeMax_all_le.
cv-cut: Same statement as GlobalTheory.CutNum.slope_good_ge. The proof follows the Lean: Formalism.ExtensionFiltration.GoodBadCut gives the rank additivity, the inequality with the term 2 d_b log g, and mu(L_b) <= mu_max(M); GlobalTheory.CutNum.numeric does the arithmetic. The inequality with the term 2 d_b log g follows good_bad_split: phi = g(1 - e) maps L onto I <= L_b of rank d_b (map_cut_le, rk_map_cut, ker_cut), ht(L_b) <= ht(I) (size_maximal_slope), and Formalism.HN.height_image_formula bounds ht(I) by the operator norms of phi (opNormAt_le, at most g) times the height htQ of L/L_g, which is ht(L)/ht(L_g) as L_g is saturated (log_htQ). Remark cv-cut-index gives the shorter index count, which is not the Lean's.

cv-mass: Formalism.HermitianLatticesTheory.mass sums over a chosen set of class representatives if one exists and is 0 otherwise; an infinite stabilizer has Nat.card 0 and contributes 1/0 = 0. In the genus (SameGenus) the localization is at the submonoid hcompl p of elements s with s and its conjugate outside p, and the local isometry is required to be a global isometry g in U(h). massI D M is the mass of the standard lattice over the host field E.
cv-siegel-mass-ratio: SiegelMassRatioCM, proved by standardMassRatio_of_modelMassRatio from GlobalTheory.Mass.siegelMassRatio_holds. A special case of the mass formula of Gan-Hanke-Yu (ratio for standard unimodular lattices, K/F unramified at all finite primes). IsCMUnram asks for a totally complex K whose star is complex conjugation at every embedding, and the condition on theta; F is the fixed field of star. Lambda_K(M) is a tprod over maximal ideals, equal to 1 in the Lean if the product is not multipliable; for M >= 3 it converges. Comparison with the published formula: the Lean's mass is sum 1/|Aut|, which is the mass of Gan-Yu [GY00, Theorem 10.20] for a totally definite form (the volume of the quotient of G(F tensor R) by Gamma_g for the Haar measure of total mass 1 on the compact group). Their formula, mass(L) = tau(G) d_F^{n^2/2} |O_F/d_{K/F}|^{n(n+1)/4} prod_{i <= n} ((i-1)!/(2 pi)^i)^{[F:Q]} / prod_v beta_v, with tau(U) = 2 (Kottwitz, Ono) and beta_v^{-1} = prod_{j <= n} L_{F_v}(j, eta^j) at the places unramified in K, gives the formula displayed in the text when K/F is unramified at every finite prime; this specialization was checked against Terakado and Yu, Mass formulas and the basic locus of unitary Shimura varieties (arXiv 2210.04054), proof of Theorem 2.3.4, equation (2.6) and the local densities after it. With |d_K| = d_F^2, the ratio for n = M and M - 1 is d_F^{M - 1/2} ((M-1)!/(2 pi)^M)^{[F:Q]} L_F(M, eta^M), which is the Lean's right side ((M-1)! (v_K/pi)^M)^{[F:Q]} (2 v_K)^{-[F:Q]/2} Lambda_K(M), since (v_K/pi)^{M[F:Q]} = |d_K|^{M/2} (2 pi)^{-M[F:Q]} and (2 v_K)^{-[F:Q]/2} = |d_K|^{-1/4}. So the Lean's statement, for M >= 3, follows from the published formula. GHY01 proves Shimura's exact formula for maximal lattices, which include the unimodular I_n here.
cv-transference: ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.T0.transference_dual, for the lattice spanned by a basis b of R^N, with the dual described by integrality of the inner products with the b_j. It is proved by gtE_main, by induction on N: a short vector of the dual lattice by Minkowski's theorem (gtB_dual_short), a primitive vector (gtC_prim) and the projection of the lattice to the orthogonal complement of that vector (gtD_lat). The bound N^2/lambda is weaker than Banaszczyk's bound N/lambda (Ban93), which the Lean does not use.

The Lean states Step 3 as sum_k |tau(v_{i,k})|^2 <= (2 f^{3/2} M^2 rd_E)^2, with f = fdeg E = [E:Q]/2. Step 4 is euclidean_basis_exists and GlobalTheory.SelfDualClasses.norm_herm_le. cv-volume-mass: MainStatements.Tam.vol proves MainStatements.Tam.VolSt, which is the statement given, for a definite datum D, a Hermitian space V : HSp D with V.SigOK (the signature condition, which here supplies the self-dual lattice) and signature (P,Q) at every place, a Haar measure mu, a fundamental domain for GQ V, the real-part homomorphism rp to the product of the U(P,Q), and measures m with IsMinf (density minfDensity r = 2^(-r(r-1)/2) for the measure IsOmegaLeb on the Lie algebra). The stabilizer K_V is Stab V, which the statement StabSt identifies with KM V 1. vol U(r) is ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.DS.volU. The Lean proves the identity from GlobalTheory.Glob.vol_eq_massI_all_sig (the volume D.vol W equals massI D (P+Q) in every signature), whose proof uses the definite case (mass_volume_identity_of_class_decomp, genusMassStd_all, doubleCosets_mass), the opposite form for signature (0,1), and for rank at least 2 GlobalTheory.T.vol_eq_mass_selfDual_rank_ge_two with Conclusion2 from CompanionTheory.HU.mass_ratio_under_volume (siegel_mass_rank_one). An earlier draft treated it as a standard result, the mass formula of Gan-Hanke-Yu expressed as a volume identity; the normalization of the measures was not checked against the published formulas, so the citation does not establish the Lean's identity. The proof follows vol_eq_massI_all_sig and Tam.vol. Step 1 is the definite case (Lemma cv-volume-mass-definite, DefiniteVolumeEqMass), the opposite form (volume_negativeDefinite_eq_opposite) and Formalism.MainNotions.StandardLattice.massRatio_of_definiteVolume, which derives the mass ratio MassRatio₂ from the volumes: the Lean does not use Theorem cv-siegel-mass-ratio here. Step 2 is Formalism.MainNotions.StandardLattice.volume_eq_mass_of_definite (VolumeEqMass₂, for P >= 2), Step 3 is GlobalTheory.Glob.vol_eq_massI_step with GlobalTheory.VolRatioUp.volRatio_up (the auxiliary space of signature (P+1,Q) comes from GlobalTheory.T.exists_hermitianSpace_with_signature, and the isometry from GlobalTheory.LandherrSignature.exists_isometry_host), all inside GlobalTheory.Glob.vol_eq_massI_of_two_le_rank. Conclusion2 for retie D is Proposition cv-volume-mass-ratio. Step 4 is the end of Tam.vol: VolTieG for retie D (GlobalTheory.Mem.retie_volTieG_and_cdScaleTie), the Haar scalar factor between mu and the normalized measure, MainStatements.Tam.V.pi_cd_eq_map (the normalized measure restricted to Stab V and pushed to the real places is the product of the D.cd.cd (P,Q)) and GlobalTheory.LowRow.CompactDualScale.isMinf_eq_volU_smul_cd (Lemma cv-volume-mass-haar). The comparison with Gan-Hanke-Yu and Prasad is Remark cv-volume-mass-literature. This is the identity between volumes and masses that the drafting pass found in the dependencies of the covolume bound; it is used in the proof, through Proposition cv-level-volume and the measure condition of Proposition cv-point-conditions(5).
cv-volume-mass-haar: Part (1) is ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.DS.PolarCoordinateComparison.omegaDensity_main: a Haar probability measure on UpqT N 0 has OmegaDensity 1/(2^(N(N-1)/2) volU N), where OmegaDensity is the limit over the sets ballU (sum of the absolute values of the entries less than t) for a measure lam with IsOmegaLeb. The Lean proves it by its own computation (volU_density) and does not cite Macdonald; the book cites Macdonald's formula [Mac80], and the covolume computation in the proof is the comparison of normalizations, done for this book. Part (2) is GlobalTheory.LowRow.CompactDualScale.isMinf_eq_volU_smul_cd, where m is a measure with Lev.IsMinf (density minfDensity N = 2^(-N(N-1)/2)) and m^c is cd.cd P Q for a structure Formalism.BasicNotions.CDHaar (Haar measures cd P Q with cd N 0 a probability measure and with the same OmegaDensity for cd P Q and cd (P+Q) 0). A Haar measure is determined by its density (omegaDensity_unique, isMinf_unique), so cd P Q is the measure m^c of the statement.
cv-volume-mass-normalized: The condition on mu is Formalism.MainNotions.StandardLattice.IsVolMeas D W P Q mu (Formalism.L2.Theta.IsVolMeasG for a signature that varies with the place), stated for every family of embeddings theta of the infinite adeles and every family of matrices A_rho with A^* J_{P,Q} A equal to the Gram matrix at rho, which are the identifications; the stabilizer is that of latHat of the coordinate lattice L0c D W. The Lean volume D.vol W of the datum retie D is GlobalTheory.Mem.Vol.trueVol: a chosen positive x with VolIs, or 1 if there is none; by Lemma cv-volume-mass-invariance(1) there is one. cv-volume-mass-local-lattices: GlobalTheory.UnramSelfDualClosed.selfDualLatticeLemmas, which is SelfDualLatticeLemmas for places v at which every prime of E is unramified (UnramifiedOrSplit), proved by GlobalTheory.UnramSelfDual.selfDualLattices: HasOrthonormalBasis, the conjugacy of self-dual lattices, and UnitVectorClaims for every unit beta. The Lean proves (1) and (2) itself (exists_frame, exists_basis, exists_unitary_lat); the book cites Jacobowitz [Jac62] for (1). For (3) the Lean uses exists_norm (units are norms), GlobalTheory.SelfDualLatticeSplit.unit_vector_splits for the decomposition and GlobalTheory.WittTransitivity.witt_transitive for the transitivity; the book's argument for the transitivity, through orthonormal bases of the two complements, is a variant of the same step. UnitVectorClaims also states that U(h) acts transitively on all vectors of norm beta, that each lies in a self-dual lattice and has a self-dual lattice in its complement, and that the stabilizer of x in K_L is isomorphic by restriction to the unitary group of the complement lattice; these are the last clause of (3) and part (4), which are not used here, with short proofs in the text (Witt's theorem and the decomposition of (3)) where the Lean has its own (witt_transitive and the lemmas of SelfDualLatticeActions). Comparison with Jacobowitz [Jac62]: he classifies Hermitian lattices over local fields by their Jordan decompositions; for an unramified quadratic extension (or a split algebra) a unimodular lattice has an orthonormal basis. The Lean's (1) is this special case, proved its own way.
cv-volume-mass-invariance: (1) is GlobalTheory.Mem.Vol.volIs_trueVol, from GlobalTheory.T.exists_isUnitaryAdelicVolumeMeasure (existence), GlobalTheory.Mem.VolUnique.volMeas_unique (uniqueness), GlobalTheory.T.fundamentalDomain_unitaryAdelic_exists_measure_eq (fundamental domains exist and have the same measure) and GlobalTheory.T.finiteVolume_adelicUnitaryQuotient (finiteness, proved in the Lean; the book cites Borel and Harish-Chandra [BHC62]); with GlobalTheory.Mem.Vol.volTieG_of_trueVol it gives VolTieG and VolTie for retie D. Independence of the identifications is built into IsVolMeas, which asks the condition for all of them. (2) is GlobalTheory.VolumeIndep.latticeIndependence (exists_conj gives k with k L-hat = L'-hat, and isVolMeas_reLat uses the right invariance of mu); (3) is GlobalTheory.VolumeIndep.volumeInvariance (isVol_of_isometry). Both are parts of IsometryTransportFrames.VolIndep, through GlobalTheory.VolIndepClosed.volIndep.
cv-volume-mass-landherr: GlobalTheory.LandherrSignature.exists_isometry_host: two HSpaces over the host field with SigOK, equal ranks and equal signatures at every embedding are isometric. GlobalTheory.UnitPerp.exists_isometry gives the isometry with the diagonal form diagForm, whose first P signs are positive. Both rest on GlobalTheory.LocalQuad.landherr_of_hasseNormSt with the Hasse norm theorem GlobalTheory.QNorm.hasseNormSt and congr_signMatrix, which use the self-dual lattice for the local determinants; the Lean proves the form of Landherr's theorem [Lan36] that it needs. Comparison: Landherr classifies nondegenerate Hermitian spaces over a quadratic extension E/F of number fields by their dimension, their signatures at the real places of F and the class of the determinant in F^x modulo norms from E. The Lean's landherrSt is the special case of two spaces with equal signatures whose determinants agree modulo local norms everywhere, combined with the Hasse norm theorem; exists_isometry_host is a consequence for spaces with unimodular lattices.

It is proved by over_of_bases from the diagonal basis of exists_isometry and hasComplement_of_basis. The lattice L is the span of that basis, in general different from the given lattice of W.

cv-volume-mass-unfolding: GlobalTheory.UnfoldingObj.unfolding proves LatticeTensorUnfolding.Unfolding D: UnfoldAt under HidaSetting (which includes the hypothesis 3 <= rank W) and the condition that the lattice of W' is L meet x-perp. It comes from GlobalTheory.T.unitaryUnfolding_volume_vectorStabilizer with the quotient measure formulas GlobalTheory.T.quotientMeasure_integration_formulas_unimodular, the Haar properties GlobalTheory.T.adelicUnitaryGroupHaarProperties_proof, and GlobalTheory.StabOrbit.stabTransitive (OrbitConcl: K_L is transitive on the vectors of norm beta in L-hat, the set of g_f with g_f^{-1} x in L-hat is H_f K_L, and K_L meet H_f equals K_{L'} meet H_f), which comes from the local lemmas of Lemma cv-volume-mass-local-lattices. The archimedean integral I is the integral over RCosets j for a quotient measure (IsQuotMeasure), required for every choice of the identifications, the embedding j and the map o (IsInfQuotIntegral).
cv-volume-mass-siegel-weil: CompanionTheory.HU.sw1b2 proves Formalism.MainNotions.StandardLattice.SW1b2 for every CM extension (IsCMExt) and nondegenerate Hermitian matrix J, by the Lean's own argument (OneVector.siegel_one_vector, EulerPos.euler_pos, ThetaLint.theta_lint_eq); it enters through CompanionTheory.HU.siegel_mass_rank_one. SW1b2 quantifies over all Haar measures mu with their fundamental domains, all characters psi with IsCharAF, and all self-dual measures and fibre families (IsFibreFamily, which includes the continuity of the fibre integrals on the nonzero values), and asserts that the local factors are multipliable and the identity in [0, infinity]. The book states it as Siegel's formula in Weil's form [Wei65]. Comparison of normalizations: Weil's formula for the action of the unitary group on the quadric h(x,x) = beta (convergent here since M >= 3) integrates the theta series over U(h)(F)\U(h)(A_F) for the Haar measure of total mass 1, which is the division by mu(F) in the Lean, so the left sides agree for every Haar measure mu. On the right Weil uses the Tamagawa measure of the adelic quadric, the product of the local measures |theta|_v of an invariant gauge form theta = omega/dq, without convergence factors since the local factors converge absolutely. The Lean's local fibre measures are quotients dx_v/dt_v of measures self-dual for psi_v(Tr h) and psi_v(st); these differ from |omega|_v and |dt|_v by |c|_v^{1/2} and |c'|_v^{1/2} for constants c, c' in F^x (the discriminant of the trace pairing in a basis and the conductor of psi), whose products over all places are 1 by the product formula. So the product of the Lean's local factors is Weil's Tamagawa measure, and the Lean's identity is Weil's formula for these test functions. The Lean's statement is slightly more general in its test functions: Phi_infinity is any measurable function with values in [0, infinity] and the local Phi_v any nonnegative locally constant compactly supported functions, where Weil takes Schwartz-Bruhat functions; and it allows every fibre family with continuous fibre integrals. It is proved in the Lean itself.
cv-volume-mass-local-density: GlobalTheory.LatticeDensityClosed.selfDualLatticeDensity, which is SelfDualLatticeDensity, through localDensity_of_selfDualLatticeLemmas: the volumes of the lattice and of O_v are dualIndex^(-M) and dualIndex^(-1/2) with dualIndex = q_v^c (IsDualExp), and the fibre value is densityValue N q eta M = N^(1/2-M)(1 - eta^M q^(-M)). The proof in the book follows the Lean: exists_coords (orthonormal coordinates), fibre_mass_mul_units_eq (the fibre mass is the same for all units), and the count ncard_sum_binary_form_ne_zero. The Lean also states that the fibre mass is constant near beta and equals every continuous density there; these are not used here.
cv-volume-mass-euler-product: GlobalTheory.DensityProductClosed.eulerProductOfDensities, which is EulerProductOfDensities, from GlobalTheory.T.cm_localDensities_productFormula: CharsAreTwists (a standard character exists and every character is a twist of it), DifferentProduct (nIdx of the standard character is the norm of the local different, and these multiply to |disc F|), |disc F| = dF E = (2 vInv E)^(fDeg E), LValue (the factors eulerInv^(-1) have product lValEta E M) and DensityProduct for every character, with a factor |a|_infty^(M-1/2) for the twist by a. The book states the case of the standard character, a = 1, which is the one ratio_of_setting uses.
cv-volume-mass-archimedean: GlobalTheory.RealPlaceMeasuresProof.realPlaceMeasures, which is RealPlaceMeasures = SelfDualMeasures, SphereVolume and QuotientMeasure, with dx = 2^(P+Q) volume (ActionCoordinates.dx) and cM M = (2 pi)^M/(M-1)!. The Lean's herm is linear in the first variable; q and the trace pairing are the same. Part (3) is QuotientMeasure, with s(y)^{-1} x0 = y and f(iota g' s y), which MeasurePreservingGlue.quotient_iff derives by inversion from GlobalTheory.CompactDualQuot.quotFormula (s(y) x0 = y and f(s y iota g')); the proof follows this. quotFormula reduces to a basis vector (exists_unitaryBlockEmbedding_onto_stabiliser, orthogonalComplement_unitary_embedding_conj_block); invariant_measure_quadric_mul_haar_stabilizer gives the constant kappa, which the text cites to the uniqueness of invariant measures on homogeneous spaces (Folland, section 2.6), the Lean proving it itself; const_mul_density proves kappa a = a' from the densities at the identity, in the four steps (i) to (iv) of the text, through the computations of Lemma cv-volume-mass-density-gauges; and formula_base compares with the compact case through positiveDefiniteUnitSphereMass_proof. The Lean states (3) for every perpendicular frame (IsPerpFrame) and every measurable section s, and the lemma for all P and Q, as the text does (c_M is defined for M >= 1; for M = 0 parts (2) and (3) are vacuous).
cv-volume-mass-density-gauges: The computations behind const_mul_density, each a Lean statement proved in the archive: (1) is CompactDualQuot.ballU_props and tanBall_props (homogeneity of the sublevel sets of the gauges, through addHaar_sublevel) with T.unitaryExpLieBall_comparable_entryGauge (ExpBallCompare.expBall_compare; expBall r is exp B_r); (2) is T.hermitianNormFibreMeasure_eq_polar_coordinates (FibrePolar.fibre_eq_polar, with polarPt the map p); (3) is T.quadricPointGauge_polarCoordinates_compare_tangentGauge (PolarCompare.polar_compare); (4) is T.unitaryLie_volume_ball_split_basis_vector (OmegaSplit.omega_split); (5) is T.exists_tangent_borelSection_quadric (TangentSection.exists_tangent_section, with tanMat the negative of the reflection qrefl exchanging e0 and -y, times flipAt); (6) is T.quadricPointGauge_section_mul_block_compare (SectionGaugeCompare.gauge_section_mul_block) with CompactDualQuot.ptGauge_act_le; (7) is T.tendsto_sublevel_density_prod_measure (SublevelDensity.tendsto_prod_density). The Lean's gauges are gauge (the l1 norm of g - 1), l1, ptGauge and tanGauge; the coordinate y_0 is the index e none of a sign-compatible bijection e, and iota_0 is a block embedding (IsBlockEmb). ThmUSt: V a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, A : PolAV over FractionRing V with HypS A.A A.L (group endomorphisms w and wd with w * wd = 1 in the group law, L ≅ cubeLB (1, w) L and cubeLB (fst >> w, snd) L ≅ cubeLB (fst, snd >> wd) L), G a commutative semi-abelian group scheme over V whose closed fibre is an extension SplitExt with IsGt, and gen : G_K ≅ A.A a group isomorphism; the conclusion is a DegData over (V, maximal ideal) and a Unif with U.gen = gen. The degeneration data are Out.DegData (DegPre: a PolAV P over V with rig, a cubical structure and sym, X free of finite rank, c : X -> P(V) additive, psi a generator over K of the pullback of P.L^(-1) along c chi; PsiEven, TauBimult, psi_pos and psi_tendsto), and Unif is UnifPre (G smooth and separated, gen, a rigidified cubical symmetric line bundle extending L, coordinates GtCoord at each thickening R/I^(e+1), with q onto the thickened abelian part, kernel the split torus of X, and line bundle data) with ExpBij k for every k >= 1 (sections of L^k over the generic fibre correspond bijectively to their expansions). UTorsSt: for such data and uniformization, F algebraically closed over FractionRing V and k >= 1, there is f from QkPt D F k with QkToAkU, onto the k-torsion, with fibres the classes of QkPt.Equiv, additive for QkAdd, and with WeilQkIs corresponding to WeilIs. The published results are Mumford's construction (Mum72) and its converse in Faltings-Chai, Chapters II and III, for principally polarized split degenerations over complete normal bases; they need no condition like HypS on (A, L), which the Lean statement adds, so the Lean statement is a special case. The text describes the data and the uniformization at the level of detail of Theorem cv-model-toroidal-degeneration.

The published results are the theory of degenerations of Faltings-Chai, Chapters II and III, with Mumford's construction (Mum72) over complete normal noetherian bases, and its form for PEL data with level structures in Lan13, Chapters 4 and 5; the Lean statement is the special case of a complete local base with a principal polarization at the generic point, with (3) added.
cv-model-literature: A remark comparing Theorem cv-model-toroidal with the literature; no Lean declaration corresponds to it. The Lean does not use toroidal compactifications for these models (see the note on cv-model-toroidal). The citations: Faltings-Chai, Chapters IV and V, for the toroidal compactifications of A_{g,n} over Z[zeta_n, 1/n] and their projectivity; Chapters II and III for degeneration data and Mumford's construction (Mum72); Lan13 for PEL data with good reduction. Comparison: these sources give toroidal compactifications with the properties (1) and (2) of Theorem cv-model-toroidal in the cases they treat; the theorem's models, built from theta constants, are related to them in kind and are not a special case of a published statement.

Property (5) is fibre_power_free_conj_injective (ConjInj), reached through GermFam.exists_residue_germ. The paragraph on functions on the fibre powers is powFns_of_abelian_generic = PositivityTheory.HtPt.Cf.pow_fns, the hypothesis PowFns of the construction. The proof follows GermSystem.main: g_eta is the GermAt g0 of exists_germ (germ_aff at the image of xi, exists_factor, exists_bc); for a point p, h_z is the GermAt gA of germ_aff in exists_loc, h_z tensor F_c(Z) is gK p (its dimension is d by loc_aux0 with germ_univ), g_z is g p, the base change of gA to the stalk (st_factor, eq_mul_inverse_pow, IsBC.cancel), and (phi_z, psi_z, lambda_z) is exists_cmp g0 (gK p) with Cmp.iso. The isomorphism V = F_c(Z)^n is lieM g0 (pt v is the tangent vector gd g0 v), with lieM_dir and lieM_act (gd_act); the Lie algebra at z in (1) is M.lat p, and lat_eq computes it from (g p).basis, comb_map and dir = key_dir (coord_tan). Property (2) is key_gen and property (3) is key_loc with the open set U p of exists_loc (stdLat_comp, transH_surj). At residue characteristic l the book writes the reduction of (4) in HodgeFreeStalk.at_point (formal_germ_base_change, hchar_map, then hfree_of_map = free_module_nakayama_descent: int_descent and abstract_descent descend freeness from k to the residue field by faithful flatness, lift_basis lifts the basis through the determinant) and that of (5) (formal_germ_base_change). The hypothesis FibPF of germ_system_height_free is model_fibres_power_free, Lemma cv-germs-principal-fibres. The paragraph on the Hodge module at a principal point follows hfree_geom: the abelian quotient, its lattice and Z are abelian_quotient_of_power_fns (the structure AbQuot), abelian_quotient_lattice (IsDiff and the lattice Λ with P and j) and abelian_quotient_bilinear (the matrix Z), Lemma cv-germs-abelian-quotient; exists_finite_kernel_nonzero is Theorem cv-germs-kernel-degree; proper_multiplication_kernel = lemF_ker_order_dvd is the paragraph's derivation of the divisibility of dim A_a by l^{d_a}, from proper_group_germ_finite_subscheme (Lemma cv-germs-kernel-hopf, the Hopf algebra A' with D and T), primitive_derivation_pairing (Lemma cv-germs-hopf-count) and finrank_ker_rhoH_le (Lemma cv-germs-kernel-pairing, with Wd); lattice_kernel_rank_bound_norm is Lemma cv-germs-lattice-kernel and exists_free_basis_of_kernel_rank_le_norm_valuation is Lemma cv-germs-free-criterion. The chart g_0 is exists_formal_germ_local with proper_has_power_fns; the counting is numeric and natDegree_charpoly_pow, and the two kernel comparisons are finrank_ker_gauge and ker_bound, Lemma cv-germs-kernel-bound. In the Lean, given by Mumford's construction is the structure PELUnif: degeneration data D : Out.DegData R I (whose DegPre has a polarized abelian scheme P : PolAV over R with the fields ample and ktriv, the latter K(L) trivial over R, and the character group X), the generic fibre A, and a uniformisation U : Out.Unif I D A t.G with U.LG = t.PP. For each e, U.gt e : GtCoord is an extension q of the abelian scheme modulo I^(e+1) by the split torus with character group X (q flat, surjective and affine, i its kernel), and U.w e is an isomorphism of the line bundle of G modulo I^(e+1) with the pullback of L along q. unif_pf takes e = 0, base-changes along R/I = residue field, and gets the triviality of K over the residue field from ktriv by kTriv_pull. In Faltings-Chai the same data appear as the Raynaud extension of G, whose formal completion along the closed fibre is that of G, with the line bundle pulled back from an ample line bundle on the abelian part, and the polarization of the abelian part induced by the principal polarization of G (Chapters II and III); Mumford's construction (Mumford 1972) inverts the passage to these data. The Lean's form records the formal completion level by level, as the isomorphisms modulo I^(e+1), and the principality of the abelian part as KTriv; only the level e = 0 is used here. The Lean takes PELUnif as given; the existence of the data is property (2) of Theorem cv-model-toroidal (Model.N3, from LN.UnifPrime.exists_pelUnif).

cv-moriwaki-bigness: MoriwakiBigStatement, proved outright by moriwakiBig_of_classicalTheorems from resolution with coordinates (resK), the arithmetic intersection system built from Poincare-Lelong, and density of curves. It is stated in a concrete model: an arithmetic variety is the vanishing locus of the multihomogeneous coordinate ideal of a point y of a product of projective spaces, with Birational y; a Hermitian line bundle is a HermLine (a multidegree and a metric on the cone); the volume is arVolP, a limsup of log counts of small sections in the chart lattice. Semipositivity is relative to an ideal P0 contained in the coordinate ideal, and the intersection numbers come from an abstract IntersectionSystem satisfying IsIntersectionSystem. The inequality is the published nef case of arithmetic Hilbert-Samuel; the Lean's hypotheses match it. The reference Mor09 was checked against Crossref: Moriwaki, Continuity of volumes on arithmetic varieties, J. Algebraic Geom. 18 (2009), no. 3, 407-457, doi 10.1090/S1056-3911-08-00500-6 (the draft's doi ended in -7, and the plan cited J. Amer. Math. Soc. 22).

cv-origin-intersection-poincare-lelong: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Hypotheses₂.PoincareLelongInv, an input that the Lean takes from the literature: it is a hypothesis of SelfIntersectionVolumeEstimates.topCovolSlim2_use_alt_alt (Theorem cv-covolume-bound-from-literature, 'the Poincaré-Lelong formula'), passed to PositivityTheory.HtPt.Ah.ais. For IsArithVar P (n + 2), smooth and conjugation-invariant L, A and B with B.a = 0, and IsSectionOn P A s (s multihomogeneous of the multidegree of A, which is in N^K, and s not in P): ptsIntegral P (Fin.cons (log h_B) (pot L)) (logNorm A s) equals the finite sum over the W in divSupp P s with IsHorizontal W of multAt (P + (s)) W times ptsIntegral W (pot L) (log h_B), minus ptsIntegral P (Fin.cons (log h_A) (pot L)) (log h_B). ptsIntegral P phi g is the integral of g against the Monge-Ampere density of the potentials phi over the complex points, computed through a projection (note on Definition lit-multiprojective); the text writes the potentials log h as first Chern forms. Comparison: on a resolution of singularities of the complex points this is the Lelong-Poincare equation of currents [Dem12, Chapter III, Section 2], which Theorem cv-tail-poincare-lelong states, and the Lean proves, on a compact complex manifold; the form on the possibly singular complex points of an arithmetic subvariety is not proved in the Lean.

cv-proportionality-mumford: GlobalTheory.T.uniformised_degree_polynomial_antisymmetric = PB.anSys_proportional, under PB.Inputs: for a finite type Psi (possibly empty), natural numbers N and j <= N, and S : AnSys D (Psi x Fin N) with D = antisymDegree Psi N that is uniformised of type j, there is v > 0 with toWt S.degPoly = C v * antisymDelta Psi N. The text states these hypotheses; Definition cv-proportionality-analytic-system allows Psi empty and every N, and the lemmas of the proof allow j = 0 and d = 0, as their Lean versions do. PB.Proportional, proved by GlobalTheory.T.proportional' (PB.proportional) from anSys_proportional and degFl_eq, adds the hypotheses Nonempty Psi and 2 <= N and says more: degFlPoly = C c * antisymDelta with c > 0, and toWt S.degPoly = C (volOf S) * degFlPoly with volOf S > 0; so v_S = c * volOf S there. toWt substitutes the gaps lambda_i - lambda_{i+1}, with lambda_{N+1} = 0, for the variables, and degPoly integrates mixed Monge-Ampere measures of the smooth potentials th. Mumford's theorem gives this for the automorphic line bundles of a locally symmetric variety with its good invariant metrics; the Lean proves it its own way, for any system with period charts to the flag domain, and the constant c comes from degFlPoly, the degree polynomial of the flag variety, which is a multiple of Delta by the Weyl dimension formula. Since Mumford's theorem is not stated for such systems, the text no longer cites it as the proof: the proof follows anSys_proportional (AnSys.mIntegrable_potH_and_mInt_eq_degNum from Inputs.convergenceSigned and eventually_mInt_potT for the passage to the singular metrics, then uniformised_potential_integral_formula = proportional_on_uniformised = PositivityTheory.Xgp.t_per_int for the computation in the charts), and the comparison with Mumford is Remark cv-proportionality-literature. In t_per_int, U is S minus the boundary (IsNull for its complement), the multilinear expansion is PB.mInt_sumPot_expand (GlobalTheory.T.monge_ampere_integral_multilinear_expansion) with the second derivatives from per_int.c2at, the pointwise identity is t_per_point at almost every point of each chart, the positivity of the integral at the flag immersion point uses the continuity of the density there (per_int.dens_cont) and the positivity of Lebesgue measure on open sets, and t_poly_delta turns the identity of values for all c into the identity of polynomials toWt(formPoly) = C v * antisymDelta, which the text states as an identity of values for all lambda. The integral is taken with the partition of unity chosen by mInt.
cv-period-monge-ampere: ReciprocityTheory.AnForm.levi is (D^2 phi(w,w) + D^2 phi(iw,iw))/4, the Levi form of the text; hessC is the complex Hessian; mdisc is (1/d!) times the alternating sum, so maDens = d! (2/pi)^d Re mdisc is the density of the text. The Lean takes the real part, which is the whole value for Hermitian matrices. M.locDens evaluates maDens on the potentials centred at the point of the chart (LocPot.phi x), and M.mInt sums over the charts of a FinHolAtlas the integrals against a ChartPartition chosen once (it is 0 if none exists, and one exists by M.existsPartition). The description as the density of dd^c phi_1 ^ ... ^ dd^c phi_d is the usual normalization and is not used by the Lean.

The proof follows agree_cauchy: intersection_difference_telescoping_integral writes the change from t to t' as integrals of phT a t - phT a t', and monge_ampere_regularization_log_log_bound (ConvergenceRateStatement, proved by Giv.convergenceRate_holds from the tail bound Giv.tailBound_holds) bounds them by C' agreeRate t, with agreeRate t = (log log (1/t))^2 / log (1/t) <= 4 s at t = exp(-1/s^2). cv-tail-shells: ReciprocityTheory.AnForm.P.tail_shells (TailShellsStatement), proved by lintegral_log_tail_shells_le with the shells {2^j R <= f}, as in the text. The Lean's integrand is ENNReal.ofReal (log f), a lower integral, which is log f on {f >= R} since log f >= 1 there. cv-tail-cutoff: ReciprocityTheory.AnForm.P.cutoff (CutoffStatement), with v = regMax 1 ![u, -M] - 1/2. The Lean's regMax eta is the integral of the maximum of t_j + eta h_j against the product of the normalized smooth bump ktheta supported in [-1/2, 1/2], that is Demailly's regularized maximum [Dem12, Chapter I, Section 5] with all parameters eta/2; the Lean proves its properties itself (regMax_thm for RegMaxStatement, regMaxLevi_thm for RegMaxLeviStatement, in PshRegMax.lean). cv-tail-situation: The data shared by TailBoundStatement, EnergyBoundStatement and PoincareLelongStatement: a compact Hausdorff space X with a finite holomorphic atlas A, a potential L with a section s (IsSection), IsSNC A L s m W (near each point s is a nowhere vanishing holomorphic function times a product of powers z_i^(m k) of coordinates, the W k being the components) and logNormSec L s <= 0. The text's r is rW L s = exp 1 - 2 logNormSec L s. On bdry s the Lean's rW equals exp 1, since the Lean's log 0 is 0, which is why the Lean writes bdry s union {R <= rW L s}; the text's {r >= R} lies off the boundary. A closed real (1,1)-form is a LocPot with IsPotential (smooth local potentials whose differences are real parts of holomorphic functions); positive definite and semipositive are IsPosPot and IsPsh. The measure omega_1 ^ ... ^ omega_d is maMeasure, and the integral of a function against a product of forms is mInt.
cv-tail-poincare-lelong: ReciprocityTheory.AnForm.M.poincareLelong (PoincareLelongStatement, proved by PLAux.pl_global) for X of dimension e + 1, with atlases B k of dimension e on the W k whose inclusions are holomorphic; the integrability is logNormIntegrable (MIntegrable A Psi (logNormSec L s) for all potentials Psi). cv-tail-energy: ReciprocityTheory.AnForm.P.EnergyBoundStatement, proved by GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Giv.tailEnergyBound with C_E = |exp 1 * mInt Theta 1 - 2 mInt Theta (logNormSec L s)| + 2|K|. The first display is TailBoundAlt.lintegral_rW_le (an inequality in the Lean), the masses are equal by massIndep, and K is from tailTelescope (tailTelescopeSucc), the sum of the K_j of the text; each step is tailEnergyStep, with C_j from TailBoundAlt.exists_psh_chern_bound, the Poincare-Lelong formula poincareLelong, and mInt_lower, mInt_nonpos for the positivity steps.
cv-tail-bound: ReciprocityTheory.AnForm.P.TailBoundStatement, proved by GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Giv.tailBound_holds with C = 16 max(C_E, 0), C_E from tailEnergyBound. The steps are those of the text: M = C_1 log R' + 2, v_i from cutoff, maMeasure_congr_open on V = {y not in bdry s, rW L s y < R'}, equal total masses by massIndep and maMeasure_thm, tail_transfer, bdry_null for mu'(bdry s) = 0, the Markov step with tailEnergyBound, and tail_shells for the second bound. cv-tail-uniform: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Giv.tail_uniform, applied to tailBound_holds, for one e-tuple of singular weights and regularizations (IsSingWeight, IsRegFamily) at a time; the text takes the maximum over the finitely many tuples. cv-condition-comparison: PB.Coefficients, proved by GlobalTheory.T.coefficients' = PB.Top.coefficients. The bound for words is realisation_height_independence = PB.abs_num_sub_num_le, for Realis.num, with C2 = (D+1) 2^D wordBound S thH; the coefficient bound adds weighted_polynomial_homogeneous_coeff_bound, with constant Cst * card(Option (Psi x Fin N))^(D+1). The hypotheses are VertClose P T alpha (Re.line a t) (Re'.line a t), NefAt P p for H.a, ref a + H.a and ref' a + H.a, and SamePot for H and thH, as in RealTower.RefLinked. cv-nef-positivity: The first clause of GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.PB.NefPol, proved by nefPol, for the special case of an analytic system of type (Psi, N). A PolAV is an abelian scheme A of relative dimension g with a line bundle L that is rigidified along the zero section (Rigidified), symmetric locally on S (Sym), relatively ample in the Lean's form RelAmple (over each affine U some L^N has sections whose nonvanishing loci are affine, cover A_U and give closed embeddings into affine spaces), and KTriv, which says that the group scheme K(L) is trivial, so that L defines a principal polarization. The archive proves it as LocalFrame.secBaseChange_of_secTwist from the law SecTwistSt, through AbLaw.AllLaws.laws_of_h0_eq_one (all the laws from h^0(L) = 1 over fields), PowBasis.exists_basis_pow and SecTwist.finrank_of_isSecBasis, about 22,900 lines with what they use; it is also the field secBaseChange of GlobalTheory.abelianSchemeLaws_all. The text cites Mumford, and the Lean's statement follows from the published results. On a geometric fibre L is ample (from RelAmple) with K(L) trivial (from KTriv, which quantifies over all rings), so chi(L)^2 = deg phi_L = 1; the vanishing theorem and the Riemann-Roch theorem of [Mum70, section 16, p. 150] give H^i(L^n) = 0 for i > 0 and h^0(L^n) = chi(L^n) = n^g chi(L) = n^g (an ample bundle has index 0, as used on p. 161, by the Corollary on p. 159 and Serre's vanishing theorem). Then the Theorem of [Mum70, section 5, p. 46] (for Y = Spec A noetherian and F coherent and flat over A, a finite complex K of finitely generated projective A-modules with H^p(X x_Y Spec B, F (x)_A B) = H^p(K (x)_A B) for all A-algebras B, functorially) and its Corollary 3 (p. 53; Y need not be reduced) show that K is split exact in positive degrees and that H^0(K) is projective of rank n^g with H^0(K) (x)_A R the sections over A_R for every A-algebra R, as at the end of the proof of Corollary 2 (p. 52). On an affine V on which H^0(K) is free a basis b gives the Lean's statement. The locators are those of the 1970 Oxford edition (section 5, Cohomology and base change, pp. 46-54; section 16, Cohomology of line bundles, pp. 150-162). Hartshorne's Algebraic Geometry, Theorem III.12.11, gives the local freeness and the base change to points, for projective morphisms, but not the base change to every ring R, which the Lean's statement needs. The rigidification and the symmetry of L are not used by the published argument.

cv-volume-forms-finite: The text cites Harish-Chandra's finiteness theorem [HC68]: on an arithmetic quotient of a semisimple group, the automorphic forms of a given K-type that are annihilated by an ideal of finite codimension in the centre of the enveloping algebra form a finite-dimensional space. Through the uniformization, a cusp form of a fixed weight on a component is such a form for the unitary group of the Hermitian matrix of the component and its arithmetic subgroup, so the lemma is a special case. The Lean does not use Harish-Chandra's theorem and proves the statement in its own form: GlobalTheory.T.finiteDimensional_cuspSections_vanishing_offDomain (= CuspSecFinData.finiteDimensional_of_le_holSub) says that every complex space of families, over finitely many components, of sections in holSub (the span of the families of cusp forms of the given weights) that vanish off the domains of frames is finite-dimensional; vanishing off the domains is the Lean's convention for functions defined on frames only. Its proof finds, for each component, a finite set of frames on which a cusp form that vanishes is zero (exists_finite_determining_set_SS, which uses only the boundedness of the pointwise norm): the pointwise norm of a nonzero form is at least half its supremum at a frame z with X.la1 z at least a constant epsilon > 0 (exists_lower_bound_half_max_norm); such a frame is moved by Gamma_Z and the triangular group into a fixed compact set of frames (FlagMahler.mahler_compactness); after the continuous Gram-Schmidt map (GramSchmidtCont.exists_continuous_gramSchmidt) a finite net of the image of that set (CuspNet.exists_finset_rmul_near_one) contains a frame at which the pointwise norm is positive (pnorm_near_half_max), so a form vanishing on the net is zero. Restriction to the net is then an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space. The deep cover uses it in GlobalTheory.Deep.finiteDimensional_V_of_good through GlobalTheory.cuspW_finiteDimensional_of_isUnf, with reading_linearIndependent_secZ for the passage from F_Y to C.
